block-definition.comment: This block turns on (show) the watcher view on stage (if it was not already activated) of the variable with the given name (slot input). It can only access to the closest variable scope (if there different variables with the same name in different scopes) following the order 'script' -> 'sprite' -> 'global'. No errors if that variable does not exist.
block-definition.translations: ca:mostra la variable _ es:mostrar variable _ pt:mostra a variável _ de:zeige var _

block-definition.comment: This block sets the given value (last input) to the variable named with the name givent (var input). It looks for that variable following the scope order 'script' -> 'sprite' -> 'global' (the first match it finds). If that variable does not exist (in any scope) an error happens, stopping their script. You can check it before using the "does var (name) exists?" block.
block-definition.translations: ca:assigna a _ el valor _ es:asignar a _ el valor _ pt:altera _ para _ de:setze var _ auf _

block-definition.comment: This block creates new variables on the selected scope: global (for all sprites), sprite (for this sprite only) or script (only for that blocks stack) with the names given (in 'names' list). If there is already a variable with that name in that scope, it does nothing: no errors and no overwrites.
block-definition.translations: pt:cria as variáveis _ _ ca:crea les _ variables _ es:crear las _ variables _ de:erstellen _ var _

Sets the volume of every instrument, from 0 to 100%. The next note to start uses it, even during playback.
Sets the tempo in quarter notes per minute in every time signature, so a quarter note lasts 60 ÷ tempo seconds. The lowest tempo is 20.
Sets the instrument for “Play Note”, “Play Chord”, and “Open MIDI Stream” when its instrument is empty.

block-definition.s: Play Note %'Note' %'Articulation' for Duration %'Duration' and Wait %'wait'
block-definition.comment: Plays a note for a duration. Write the note as a pitch (e.g., C4, Bb3 or E#3) or as a MIDI number. Use “R” for rests. Write the duration as a name (e.g., Quarter) or as a number of whole notes (e.g., .25). Grace plays a thirty-second note. With “and Wait” on, the block waits for the duration, so notes play in sequence. With “and Wait” off, the next block runs concurrently. Marks after the note are “.” (staccato), “>” (accent), “-” (legato), and “u” (bend up a whole step). “ud” bends up and back down. Ties and glides are ignored. The arrow at the right adds Staccato, Legato or Accent from a menu.

The “with” menu at the end marks the lowest note Staccato, Legato or Accent, which marks the whole chord.

Joins a list of measures into one plain list of pairs. The “Play Tracks” block expects two or more measures to be in a section.

block-definition.s: Track: %'Type' Instrument: %'Instrument' $nl Musical Notation (Notes or Chords): %'Notation'
block-definition.comment: Reports a track for “Play Tracks” from a type, an instrument, and a list of (note, duration) pairs; a chord can take the place of a note. Loop-Melody and Loop-Chords repeat for as long as the longest track that is not a loop. If no other tracks are present, a looped track will not play. A third item added to a pair sets the loudness (e.g., pp, p, mp, mf, f or ff); adding cresc or dim (e.g., “p cresc”) changes volume gradually up to the next mark.

block-definition.s: Play Tracks %'tracks' in Time Signature %'timeSignature' and Wait %'wait' %'fromMeasure'
block-definition.comment: Plays the tracks together at the set tempo. The time signature is the number of beats per measure over the note value that gets the beat. Groups from “Import MIDI File” can replace the tracks; each keeps its own time signature and tempo. With “and Wait” on, multiple “Play Tracks” blocks can be chained together sequentially. This is helpful when composing pieces that change time signature or tempo. The arrow shows “from Measure”. If a number is entered, “Play Tracks” will begin playing from that measure. If no value is entered or if the field is hidden, the track plays from the beginning.

Runs the script in the ring and saves the music of its “Play Tracks” blocks as a MIDI, WAV, MP3, or MusicXML file. The “Play Tracks” blocks do not play. Volume settings included in the ring are incorporated into the exported file.

Reports the beats a measure's durations fill against the time signature, such as 3 of 4 beats. The top number of a time signature is the beats per measure, and the bottom number is the note that gets the beat; 4/4 holds four quarter notes and 6/8 six eighth notes. A misspelled duration makes the block report nothing.
Plays a MIDI keyboard or controller live through TuneScope on the chosen instrument until “Close MIDI Stream”. Choose a device, type part of its name, or leave it empty for the first device found.

block-definition.s: Record MIDI Stream $nl Time Signature: %'Time Signature' Smallest Note: %'Smallest Note' $nl Click While Recording: %'Click While Recording'
block-definition.comment: Records what you play on the open MIDI device. Two measures of clicks count in at the current tempo and the given time signature. Recording starts on the next downbeat. With “Click While Recording” on, the clicks go on until “Close MIDI Stream”. Timing is rounded to the smallest note. “Close MIDI Stream” saves the notes.

Stops any recording and disconnects the device. The recorded notes go into a new global variable, MIDI Capture (MIDI Capture 2, 3, … when the name is taken), as (note, duration) pairs for a “Track” block. MIDI Warnings reports notes left out, timing drift, and held notes that were cut.

Opens a MIDI file (.mid or .midi) and makes a global variable for each track. A two-staff part becomes Piano (upper) and Piano (lower), and a drum part one track per kit sound. Notes that start together become chords. MIDI File Tracks holds all the tracks, and MIDI File Tempo and MIDI File Time Signature the first values. MIDI File Groups and Track Group 1, 2, … hold the sections between tempo or time-signature changes, for “Play Tracks”. Each time-signature change starts a new set of Track variables. MIDI Warnings lists what was changed or left out. “Delete MIDI Tracks” removes these variables.
Removes the Track and Track Group variables, MIDI File Tracks, Groups, Tempo and Time Signature, and MIDI Warnings, numbered copies included.

Reports the 18 duration names with their lengths in whole notes. A dotted note is 1.5 times its plain note, and a triplet note two thirds of it. The table is built on the first run and kept in the block variable Table, for Note Duration Value and List of Note Durations.

block-definition.s: Note Duration %'Note Duration' at Current Tempo
block-definition.comment: Reports a duration's length in seconds at the current tempo, whole notes × 4 × 60 ÷ tempo. The duration may be a name, such as Quarter, a number of whole notes, such as .25, or a list of either. Grace gives a thirty-second note.

inputs.input: QuarterWhole Half Quarter Eighth Sixteenth Thirtysecond Dotted Notes={ Dotted Half Dotted Quarter Dotted Eighth Dotted Sixteenth } Triplet Notes={ Half Triplet Quarter Triplet Eighth Triplet Sixteenth Triplet }

block-definition.comment: Shows a visualization of the music on the stage, behind the sprites, based on the selected style.
Removes the visualizer from the stage.

Loads TuneScope once. It loads the primitives file, then ts_load() fetches the helper files and the piano and percussion sounds and decodes them. ts_loaded() reports true when they are ready, so later calls end after two checks. Other instruments load the first time a block uses them.

Reports the 21 note names of an octave (naturals, sharps and flats, plus Cb, Fb, E# and B#) with their MIDI numbers in octave 1, where C1 is 24. The table is built on the first run and kept in the block variable Table, for MIDI Note and Chromatic Notes.
Reports the 21 note names from Note Table.
Reports the natural note for E# (F), Fb (E), B# (C) and Cb (B). Other names come back unchanged.
Reports the MIDI number of a pitch, such as C4. A MIDI number comes back unchanged, so blocks built on this one accept either.
Reports the note name of a pitch, its first letter plus any # or b. C4 gives C, Bb3 gives Bb, and C-1 gives C.
Reports the MIDI number in octave 1 of a note name in any case, from Note Table; C gives 24 and Bb gives 34. An unknown name is an error.
Reports the octave of a pitch, everything after the note name. C4 gives 4, C#10 gives 10, C-1 gives -1, and C alone gives empty text.

Reports the pitch of a MIDI number (60 is C4), or the pitches of a list of numbers, nested lists such as chords included. Sharps, # or empty gives sharp names; Flats, b or ♭ gives flat names. All 128 names are computed on the first run and kept in the block variable Note Table, so later runs only look them up.
Reports the scale degree, 1 to 7, of a Roman-numeral chord position, I to VII, in either case, with or without °. An unknown numeral is an error.

Reports the 18 duration names from Note Duration Table.
Reports a duration's length in whole notes; Quarter gives .25. A number comes back unchanged, and a list gives a list. An unknown name is an error.
